title: Interior regularity of planar Mumford–Shah minimizers
coverage: I read every section. I checked the new core argument (Sections 4–5) line by line. Lemma 4.1 (isolating a compact piece) holds; it uses the clopen-neighbourhood fact for compact spaces. Lemma 5.2 (projection): the exterior Fourier argument rules out the log mode, which gives phi=O(1/|x|) and p=O(|x|^-2). Lemma 5.3 (translated comparison): the competitor V_R is admissible, lengths cancel exactly, and the glued-annulus error is O(R^-1/2) because ||∇v||_{L^2(B_2R)}=O(R^{1/2}) and the cutoff term has gradient O(R^-1) in L^2. The interaction integrals converge absolutely by the dyadic bound s^{1/2}·s^{-1}. Lemma 5.4 (harmonicity of the interaction): I confirmed it independently. Integrating by parts gives I_p(t) = -∫_A [F] ∂_n f(y+t) dH^1, which is plainly harmonic in t. A harmonic function with a minimum at 0 is constant, and then the coefficient of σ must vanish. This is equivalent to the Neumann condition on every translate. Jump-flux step: the test functions h'_β are admissible when the arc is only C^1, and the step uses div G=0 on the whole plane, which follows from Neumann-type variations. If one fixed directional derivative of a harmonic function is constant, the function is affine. Unique continuation then holds on the connected set O. The growth bound gives G=0, then p=0, then v is constant, so removing A strictly lowers the energy. Section 6 (assembly): the classification follows from the cited facts, namely Cor 4.4.3, the David–Léger theorem, and Bonnet–David (Thm 1.4.6). The epsilon-regularity transfer and the component-finiteness cover are fine. I did not check independently: the Section 2 reduction to a rectifiable, locally bounded pair (standard De Giorgi–Carriero–Leaci/SBV material), or the exact content of the cited De Lellis–Focardi monograph statements (Thm 2.2.3(ii), Thm 1.4.6, Cor 4.4.3, Thm 1.3.3). Those were taken as cited.
main_claim: Interior regularity for reduced absolute planar Mumford–Shah minimizers with L^∞ fidelity datum: at every point of K, K is locally a C^{1,α} arc, an arc ending at that point (crack tip), or a 120° triple junction; only finitely many components of K meet each U⋐Ω; and ∇u ∈ L^{4,∞}_loc. The key new step excludes bounded components of global generalized minimizers whose complement is connected. Fix f, translate the compact piece A together with its jump field F, and note that the resulting interaction energy is harmonic in the translation, so minimality forces it to be constant. Varying the jump on a regular arc then makes f affine, which leads to zero energy, and removing A gives a contradiction.
sibling_notes: When I checked, the family 366 board was empty. I posted a no_gap_found summary. Anyone auditing related papers should note that the decisive identity is I_p(t) = -∫_A [F] n·∇f(y+t) dH^1. Translation-harmonicity follows from that identity, and the translated configurations then satisfy the Neumann condition on every translate.
